current.text: Riley is one of many young wings and guards on a crowded Washington roster.
He is not in the projected starting five: Trae Young, Kyshawn George, AJ Dybantsa, Anthony Davis and Alex Sarr. The fifth starter spot is unclear, and many wings are competing for it.
Washington added Trae Young, Anthony Davis and AJ Dybantsa, and all three missed last season.
Experts expect Young, Davis and Dybantsa to take most of the usage. That leaves little for the young players and cuts into their roles.
Washington's roster is deep and flexible. A 10 or 11 man rotation is expected, with 12 or 13 players who could justify minutes.
He averaged 22.5 points in two Summer League games and shot well.
The expert does not expect his late-season value from last season to return, because Washington has too many wings and guards.
Washington is trying to compete for the play-in, so the late-season resting and minutes shifts of past years should not happen this season.

durable.text: Projections give him very few steals, a clear weakness against the player pool.
